summary: The Applicant has applied to the Committee of Adjustment (Application A1080/17TEY) for variances to the applicable zoning by-laws to permit the construction of a new three-storey detached dwelling with a rear ground floor deck, a rear third floor deck, and a rear detached garage (the "Application"). The Application requires a number of variances, including for building height, number of storeys, floor space index/gross floor area, and building length. The Application is of concern because the variances requested would result in the construction of a house that is out of character with the surrounding neighbourhood. In particular, at 10.36 metres and three-storeys in height, the proposed house is too tall. The proposal also results in an increased floor space index/gross floor area of 0.66 times the area of the lot whereas only 0.4 times the area of the lot is permitted. Furthermore, the proposed three storey dwelling has the potential for adverse impacts on neighbouring properties and the Rushton streetscape. At its hearing on March 21, 2018, the Committee of Adjustment refused the Application (the "Decision"). A copy of the Notice of Decision of the Committee of Adjustment is attached. The Applicant has now appealed the Decision to the Toronto Local Appeal Body. This Motion will give the City Solicitor, along with other appropriate City Staff, authority to attend the Toronto…
decided: City Council on April 24, 25, 26 and 27, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council authorize the City Solicitor to negotiate a settlement of the appeal of Application A1080/17TEY respecting 629 Rushton Road and authorize the City Solicitor to settle the matter on behalf of the City in the City Solicitor's discretion after consultation with the Ward Councillor. 2. In the event that a settlement is not reached, City Council authorize the City Solicitor, along with appropriate City Staff, to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body in order to oppose the variances requested in Application A1080/17TEY respecting 629 Rushton Road and to retain outside consultants, as necessary.
